newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ surpluses won't appear under National - Cullen.
newsitem.headline: NZ surpluses won't appear under National - Cullen.

text.p: Opposition Labour Party finance spokesman Michael Cullen said on Monday that surpluses of the kind projected in the New Zealand Treasury's latest forecasts would not materialise under the conservative National Party.
"I believe with a National-led government those surpluses will not appear. You cannot achieve those levels of growth without addressing the needs of the export sector," Cullen told reporters.
"It's very important that action is taken in respect of the exchange rate."
Both Labour and National are negotiating with nationalist New Zealand First, which holds the balance of power, with the aim of forming a government.
Cullen has consistently argued the currency is overvalued.
"The point that I'm making...is that unless we have direct action on the exchange rate in the near future, then you can forget about the fiscal surpluses that came out today," Cullen said.
He declined to comment on the mechanisms he would use to bring down the exchange rate.

Cullen said: "I am saying the exchange rate has to be affected directly, or you can forget about those (Treasury) forecasts. They are based on a quite unsustainable level of current account deficit, which will be accompanied by a major adjustment to this economy some time next year. So if we have a National-led government we will have smaller fiscal surpluses than if we have a Labour-led government by the year after next, and I'm very confident about that."
Treasury forecast in its December update that the government would achieve a NZ$2.49 billion budget operating surplus in the 1996-7 year, rising to $6.11 billion by 2000.
